titre_page: How to make a brick breaker game in Yop2D? | Yop2D Guide
description: Make a brick breaker game in Yop2D with no code: a paddle you move with your finger, a bouncing ball, bricks to break, score and lives with nodes.
h1: How to make a brick breaker game?
carte: Paddle moved by finger, bouncing ball, bricks to break, score and lives.
blocs: In a brick breaker, a **ball** bounces off the edges and off a **paddle** you move with your finger, and breaks **bricks**. Here we drive the ball with two small variables, **vx** (its speed to the right) and **vy** (its speed downward). When the ball bounces, we simply change the sign of the variable.
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **paddle**, at the bottom of the screen (for example 240 x 48 px, around y = 1700);
an {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} named **ball**, in the middle of the screen (for example 48 x 48 px);
bricks: {{lang:obj_prefix_image}}s at the top of the screen (for example 120 x 48 px, 9 per row to fill the 1080 px width);
two {{lang:obj_prefix_texte}} objects: **scoreText** (text « Score: 0 ») and **livesText** (text « Lives: 3 »), at the top of the screen.
This guide is written for a **1080 x 1920 portrait** game. The images (paddle, ball, bricks) can be your own drawings or free-to-use images from the Yop2D library.
Select a brick. In the inspector, field **{{lang:insp_label_tag}}**, type **brick**. Do the same for every brick.
In the left panel, open the **{{lang:panneau_ress_variables}}** section and create five variables, all with scope **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}** and type **{{lang:var_type_entier}}**:
**bricks**: the **number of bricks** in your game (for example **27**). It tells you when everything is broken;
**vx** and **vy**: starting value **0**. This is the ball's speed, set when the game starts.
One brick more or less? Just change the starting value of **bricks**. If the number is too big, you never win; if it is too small, you win too early.
Step 2: the paddle follows your finger
Add the **[[NoeudEventDoigtAppuye]]** event (it repeats as long as a finger is on the screen).
Link the two nodes, then run the game: the paddle follows your finger and never leaves the screen.

**How to read the formula?** `doigt.x` is your finger's position (« doigt » means finger). We subtract 120 (half the paddle) to center it under the finger. `clamp(…, 0, 840)` keeps it on screen: 840 = 1080 − 240 (the paddle's width).
Add the **[[NoeudEventStart]]** event, then two **[[modifier_variable]]** nodes one after the other: variable **vx** = `6`, then variable **vy** = `-9`.
Add the **[[NoeudEventChaqueImage]]** event, then **[[pousser]]**: target **ball**, **Add X**, value `=vx`, **Add Y**, value `=vy`.
Link each event to its nodes and run the game: the ball goes up and to the right, and leaves the screen.
**Negative = up.** In Yop2D, Y grows toward the bottom of the screen: **vy = -9** sends the ball upward. For a faster ball, use 8 and -12.

Right after **[[pousser]]**, we check on every frame whether the ball touches an edge. We chain three **[[condition]]** nodes, each time following the **[[lang:port_ensuite]]** output (which runs in every case).
Left edge: **[[condition]]** `=ball.x <= 0`. Output **{{lang:port_vrai}}** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**, value `=abs(vx)` (always to the right).

Right edge: **[[condition]]** `=ball.x >= 1032`. Output **{{lang:port_vrai}}** → **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**, value `=-abs(vx)` (always to the left). 1032 = 1080 − 48 (the ball's width).
Link each **[[condition]]** to the next one with its **[[lang:port_ensuite]]** output. The first one is linked to the output of **[[pousser]]**.
**Why abs?** `abs(vx)` is always a positive number. At the left edge, the ball is forced to go right, even if it touches the edge two frames in a row: it never gets stuck.
Add **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vy**, value `=-abs(vy)` (the ball goes back up).
Add a second **[[modifier_variable]]**: variable **vx**, value `=(ball.x + 24 - paddle.x - 120) / 15`.
Link the three nodes in order.

**What is the last formula for?** It measures where the ball lands on the paddle: in the middle, it goes straight up; on the left edge, it goes left; on the right edge, it goes right. The player can **aim**. (24 = half the ball, 120 = half the paddle.)
Add **[[detruire_objet]]** and choose **{{lang:noeud_objet_implique_long}}** as the target: it is the brick the ball has just touched.
Link all the nodes in order.
When the ball breaks a brick, it always bounces up or down, even if it hit the brick from the side. It is simple, and it works well in a brick breaker.
On the **{{lang:port_vrai}}** output: **[[toast]]** with the message **You win!**, then **[[attendre]]** 2 seconds, then **[[recommencer_scene]]**.
[[recommencer_scene]] puts the objects back in place and the **{{lang:var_scope_locale}}** variables back to their starting value: the game restarts with 3 lives, 0 points and all the bricks.

When the ball falls below the paddle, the player loses a life. We continue the chain from step 4: after the third **[[condition]]** (the top), add a fourth one, linked by its **[[lang:port_ensuite]]** output.
Output **{{lang:port_vrai}}** (no lives left): **[[toast]]** « Game over! », **[[attendre]]** 2 seconds, **[[recommencer_scene]]**.
Output **{{lang:port_faux}}** (lives left): **[[deplacer]]** the **ball** to X = `516`, Y = `1000`, then **[[modifier_variable]]** **vy** = `-9`, then **[[modifier_variable]]** **vx** = `6`.
**Sounds:** add **[[jouer_son]]** after **[[detruire_objet]]** (a « clack » when a brick breaks) and in the paddle event.
**Different colors:** give the same tag **brick** to all the bricks, whatever their color: a single setup is enough.
**More speed:** add **[[modifier_variable]]** `=vx * 1.02` each time a brick breaks so the game gets harder and harder.
**Sparks:** add an **[[effet_particules]]** when a brick breaks (see the guide [Particles and effects](guide:particules-effets)).
**The ball doesn't move:** check that **vx** and **vy** are changed at the start, and that **[[pousser]]** uses the formulas `=vx` and `=vy` (with the **=** at the beginning).

**The ball goes through the paddle or the bricks:** check the names (**ball**, **paddle**) and the tag **brick**, spelled the same everywhere (no capital letter). If the ball is very fast, make the bricks a little bigger or slow the ball down.

**The ball leaves the screen without bouncing:** the **[[condition]]** nodes must be linked one after the other with the **[[lang:port_ensuite]]** output, and the first one must start from **[[pousser]]**.
**You win too early or never:** the variable **bricks** must be exactly the number of bricks in the game.
**The paddle moves badly:** in the formula, `doigt.x` is the finger, not the paddle; keep the **=** at the beginning and close the parenthesis.
